editorial:
Imagine waking up and realizing you totally missed your own cult's mass suicide event. That is exactly where you find our main character, a guy who is pretty much a professional loser. He ends up teaming up with his old fake leader, and the two of them hit the road through middle America to find new followers. Along the way, they pick up some really weird people, like a military geek and a stressed-out mom. The vibe is totally chaotic and funny, focusing on a bunch of broken people trying to find a place where they actually fit in, even if it is in a fake doomsday group.

You will love how the actors play off each other, especially the constant fighting between the two leads. The pacing is quick, and the jokes land well, though some of the slower parts in the middle might feel a bit long. If you like dark humor and awkward situations, you should definitely check this out. It looks great if you can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, but renting it on Apple TV is a solid choice too. If you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your shelf is the way to go for the best quality.
endingExplained: In the end, the group realizes that their fake religion was just a way to hide from their real problems. Instead of following a crazy leader or waiting for the world to end, they decide to actually support each other as real friends. They stop trying to start a cult and choose to live their lives in the real world. It wraps up with a sweet message about finding a real family in the strangest places.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark humor and stories about weird misfits.
